newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U says '97 focus on new products.
newsitem.headline: P&U says '97 focus on new products.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn on Wednesday said its focus in 1997 would be on new products and some medicines will be launched sooner than planned.
Sales in the fourth quarter of 1996 rose by 7.5 percent to $1.9 billion and the company posted earnings per share of $0.51 on net earnings of $268 million before non-recurring items of $42 million.
P&U's chief executive Jan Ekberg said the company was satisfied with fourth-quarter earnings per share.
"However margin improvements were not up to expectations and we have many challenges ahead," Ekberg said in a statement.
"Our focus in 1997 will be to build and consolidate our position to generate longer-term strong performance."
For the full year ending December 31, the company reported a 6.1 percent rise in earnings per share to $1.90 on net earnings of $998 million before non-recurring items of $436 million.
The earnings were largely in line with expectations. A Reuter poll of 12 analysts showed expectations were for earnings per share of $1.92.
Full-year net sales rose 3.3 percent to $7.2 billion following strong new product performance and marketing synergies, the company said. Foreign exchange fluctuations had, however, a negative impact.
"The strengthening of the U.S. dollar against the Japanese yen reduced 1996 sales by two percentage points," it said.
Ekberg said the company would take dollar movements into account and that it would focus on new-product introductions, some of which are ahead of schedule.
"We will concentrate on new-product introductions, some of which are coming sooner than anticipated and on strengthening our mangement systems and ensuring that our infrastructure matches our needs.
"We also will need to take into account the uncertainties in the marketplace, including the development of a strong dollar," Ekberg said.

Regarding new drugs, the company said it filed a regulatory submission in Europe for tolterodine, which has shown promise in treating urge urinary incontinence, with a U.S. filing expected later in the year.
A number of important products are under regulatory review in different countries.

These include anti-depressant Edronax in the European Union, glaucoma treatment Xalatan filed in Japan, Mirapex for Parkinson's disease filed in Europe and the U.S., and AIDS treatment drug Rescriptor.
New drugs starting to drive sales were anti-colon cancer drug Camptosar and Xalatan, which had sales of around $59 million and about $30 million respectively, Pharmacia & Upjohn said.
The growth hormone Genotropin, the company's biggest product, was up four percent in the fourth quarter.
